reasons: The leg traded here has already been measured, and it does not pay even on the days where the claimed flow is strongest. The rationale cites the gotobi edge (+0.10 to +0.14 R, design t 3.2), but that edge is the post-fix SHORT (sell at 00:55 UTC, exit 06:00 UTC: design +0.144 R, check +0.112 R; gj-strat results/patterns_usdjpy). The same pre-declared grid also tested this hypothesis's leg: long into the 09:55 JST fix, stop 0.25 x ATR20, full costs (P1 fix-long). On gotobi days it made +0.013 / +0.007 / -0.016 R in design for 23:00 / 23:30 / 00:00 UTC entries (t 0.42 / 0.24 / -0.68; check -0.008 / +0.010 / -0.016). On all other weekdays it made -0.092 / -0.082 / -0.066 R (t -5.2 / -5.0 / -4.4; check -0.097 / -0.061 / -0.039). Every candidate day in this hypothesis is one of those 'other' days.

The pre-registered size contradicts the mechanism once it is calibrated on those numbers. Gotobi days carry only +0.05 to +0.10 R more pre-fix drift than other days (about 1-2 pips at the ~21-pip design stop; design ATR20 median 85 pips). That is no more than the round-trip cost of 0.08-0.10 R, so the leg nets about zero where settlement demand is most concentrated. A holiday on a non-gotobi date moves one ordinary day's payments, so a holiday-adjacent day should carry less extra pre-fix demand than a gotobi day, not more. Netting +0.12 R needs about +0.2 R gross (~4 pips), roughly twice the gotobi run-up, and even the +0.05 R kill floor needs more than the gotobi run-up delivers. The expectation based on the programme's own measurements is about -0.05 to 0 R.

The design does not isolate holiday-shifted ordinary demand as claimed. F.is_gotobi ignores Japanese holidays. When a gotobi date is itself a holiday (May 5 and Dec 31 every year, the 10th/15th/20th when a Happy-Monday holiday lands on them, Mar 20 equinoxes, Apr 30 in 2012/2018/2019), the shifted gotobi settlement lands on exactly the BEFORE/AFTER days this rule trades. Outcome-free calendar count: at least 41 of the 130 design 'either' days (30 of 100 in check) sit next to a holiday that falls on a gotobi date. The holiday adjustment of gotobi has also been measured on the leg that does pay. gj-strat run_gotobi_calendar moved gotobi dates on JP holidays to the previous JP business day: design +0.143 R (t 2.90) against +0.144 R (t 3.16) for the weekend-only rule, check +0.099 against +0.112, and it was not adopted. The live-leg holiday adjustment suggested in the direction note has therefore already been tested.

The precedent is weaker than stated. The atlas 'day after a US holiday' survivor is a 30-minute Sydney-clock window: 11:30-12:00 Sydney is 00:30-01:00 UTC in the southern summer and 01:30-02:00 UTC in the southern winter. For half the year it lies wholly after the fix, so it is no evidence of a pre-fix run-up on post-holiday days. It survived a 431,424-test pair scan at the scan's Bonferroni edge (mid design t 5.0); as a trade it had t 2.67 in design, 0.96 in check and 153 trades in all. The 'before' arm re-slices an atlas day type ('day before a Japan holiday', scanned on the Tokyo clock with windows ending at the fix). The scrap index asks new clock/calendar ideas for design t >= 3.7; this pre-registration expects 1.5.

Sample and power, outcome-free. The hardcoded holiday list is correct: it matches a rule-based rebuild of the statutory, substitute, citizens', 2019 enthronement, 2020/21 Olympic and bank-closure days exactly (278 weekday entries). It yields design AFTER 73, BEFORE 59, EITHER 130 days (59 more removed as gotobi) and check 56 / 45 / 100. Backing sd(R) out of the P1 tests gives about 0.55-0.75 at 0.25 x ATR20, so even the hoped-for +0.12 R gives a design t of only about 1.4 (before), 1.6 (after) and 2.1 (either). The single-side arms are not expected to reach the t >= 2 pass bar. The kill rule judges the best of 18 overlapping cells on 59-130 trades, which has a sizeable chance of clearing t >= 1 with no edge, so it tests the best point, not the surface (charter rule 7).

Concentration and the cost of the early entry. Of the 130 design days, 19 fall in year-end/New Year and 23 in Golden Week (thin, gappy markets), and 22 are Mondays whose 22:30 and 23:30 UTC entries fall on the Sunday reopen; a handful of idiosyncratic days can carry an 18-cell surface. The design median USDJPY spread is 1.0 pip at 22:30 UTC (winter 1.3, p90 2.1) against 0.6 at 23:30-00:00 UTC. The gj-strat clock scan already shows that buying USDJPY at 22:30 UTC for an hour lost -0.080 R (t -8.3) on all weekdays and -0.064 R on gotobi days in design.
reviews.revisions: None; rejected. Record in the scrap knowledge that a long into the Tokyo fix is cost-dominated on every day type tested: gotobi about 0 R; other weekdays -0.07 to -0.09 R in design and negative in check (gj-strat P1 fix-long). Also record that the gotobi holiday adjustment (previous-business-day calendar) has been measured and was not adopted. A holiday-settlement idea can only come back under three conditions. It trades the post-fix leg (short 00:55 to 06:00 UTC, where gotobi pays). It trades only days that actually receive a shifted gotobi settlement under the still-untested next-business-day convention. It is pre-registered against the gotobi short's own per-trade R. At about 4-6 such days a year it can only be judged as an adjustment to the existing gotobi leg, not as a stand-alone strategy.
reviews.notes_for_builder: Not to be built (rejected). If the Director overrides: (1) Build the holiday array with np.array(HOLIDAYS, dtype='datetime64[D]'); the list was verified against the statutory rules. (2) Missed-fix days are listed dates with F.weekday < 5. (3) Get the previous and next weekday with np.busday_offset(d, -1, roll='forward') and np.busday_offset(d, 1, roll='backward'). (4) Candidates are Mon-Fri dates not in the list with F.is_gotobi False. (5) Entry target = d + entry_utc when hh < 12, else (d - 1 day) + entry_utc; ei = np.searchsorted(m.ts, target). Skip the day if ei < 1, ei >= m.n or m.ts[ei] - target > max_delay_min. (6) Find xi the same way for d + exit_utc; skip if xi >= m.n, xi <= ei or it is late. (7) Read ATR20 at ei; that is trading day d for all three entry times, because 22:30 UTC is after 17:00 New York in both seasons. (8) Put sl_dist and entry_long on ei-1 and exit_long on xi-1. (9) Read side, entry_utc, exit_utc, sl_atr and max_delay_min from p. (10) Report results split into shifted-gotobi, year-end, Golden Week and other days.

reasons: This is the same family as dead entries, with only a participant label added. Fading the previous session's move when the next session's participants arrive is prior_fx_session_rev: fading the Asia-session extreme at the London open found no reversal even on mid prices (base reversal variant mid-to-mid about -0.001 R) and lost after costs. Tokyo-hours fades on USDJPY have also lost: the gj-strat quiet-hours Bollinger fade (22:00-06:00 UTC) made -0.062 R (t -3.4) in design and -0.068 R in check. This cycle's own lesson puts session reversal in the dead pile. Charter rule 8 requires a clearly different mechanism, and the named participants do not supply one (next reason).

The timing premise is not supported. Japanese retail margin accounts trade mostly after Tokyo working hours, which is the London afternoon and New York morning, inside the 13:00-21:00 UTC window being faded. Their documented contrarian behaviour is measured against the day's move and already acts during the New York session; it does not arrive as a burst at 09:00 JST. Importers' dollar buying concentrates into the 09:55 JST fix on settlement days (the gotobi flow); their price-sensitive buying is typically left as resting orders with Tokyo banks that fill during the fall itself. Both groups are present on both sides of the window. On Japanese holidays, which the rules do not exclude, Tokyo institutions are absent from the open altogether.

The required effect is too large relative to costs. The unconditional long in this window already loses after costs. gj-strat P1 fix-long (00:00 UTC to the 00:55 fix, all weekdays, SL 0.25 x ATR20) made -0.052 R (t -4.1), and the clock scan's buy from 00:00 to 01:00 UTC made -0.074 R (t -5.6) in design. A round trip at the Tokyo open costs about 1.65 pips on USDJPY (design median spread 0.6 / 0.5 pips at 00:00 / 00:55 UTC). On AUDJPY it costs about 2.5 pips (spread 1.5 / 1.3; the 0.9 quoted is the 2022-23 all-hours median). That is 0.08-0.10 R at 0.25 x ATR20, with design ATR20 medians of 85 and 103 pips. To net +0.06 R, the long arm needs about 3 pips gross per trade, so the first Tokyo hour would have to retrace about 5-6% of the New York move on trigger days. That implies a correlation of roughly -0.15 to -0.2 between the 8-hour New York return (sigma about 31 pips) and the next 55 minutes (sigma about 10 pips), and more at 0.5 x ATR20. Measured FX predictability here is an order of magnitude smaller: USDJPY lag-1 autocorrelation -0.002 at H1 and -0.014 at D1, and no reversal before costs at the Asia-London boundary.

The pre-registration is internally inconsistent. Outcome-free design trigger counts (signal only, no returns): USDJPY theta 0.75 long 291 / both 613, theta 1.25 long 151 / both 309; AUDJPY 303 / 632 and 162 / 311. The primary long-only arm at theta 1.25 falls below the 200-trade minimum on both markets (4 of the 8 cells per market). The claim of roughly 400 design trades per market at 1.25 sigma is wrong: it is about 310 for both sides and about 155 for longs only.

Calendar confounding and an asymmetric kill rule. About a third of the long trades fall on gotobi days (USDJPY 81 of 291 and 48 of 151; AUDJPY 100 of 303 and 52 of 162). On gotobi days JPY weakens into the 09:55 fix in every JPY cross and recovers afterwards. The long arm and the short side of 'both' therefore meet a known flow in opposite directions, and the 02:00 exit adds the post-fix reversal against the longs. The kill rule scraps only 'long <= 0 while both > 0'. The reverse pattern (long > 0, both <= 0), which unconditional drift or gotobi would produce, would be read as 'importer plus retail buying after falls', so the claimed asymmetry cannot be falsified. Large New York moves also cluster on US data, FOMC and auctions inside 13:00-21:00 UTC, and moves driven by information do not revert (prior_cb_drift; prior_cross_zfade: 2-sigma moves kept running).
reviews.revisions: None; rejected. A Tokyo-open idea should only be registered around a forced flow whose timing is set by the clock or the calendar. It must be pre-registered against the unconditional trade with the same entry, exit, stop and days, which already loses about 0.05-0.07 R here. It should exclude gotobi days and Japanese holidays. Before compute is spent, it needs a back-of-envelope check that the implied predictability (gross edge needed per trade divided by the window sigma) is plausible.
reviews.notes_for_builder: Not to be built (rejected). If the Director overrides: (1) For each trade date d (Tue-Fri), i13 = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, d-1, 13, 0) - 1, and i21 likewise for 21:00. (2) Require i >= 0, m.ts[i] < target and target - m.ts[i] <= 15 minutes. (3) M = ln(bid_c[i21] / bid_c[i13]). (4) sigma = std (ddof 1) of the previous p['vol_window'] finite M values, excluding the current day; loop over days and skip until enough history exists. (5) Trade only if |M| >= theta * sigma and M != 0; take shorts only when side == 'both'. (6) Entry bar ei = first bar at or after d + entry_utc, within max_delay_min. Put the signal and sl_dist on ei-1 and read ATR20 at ei. (7) Put exit_long / exit_short on xi-1. (8) Read theta, exit_utc, sl_atr, side, ny_start, ny_end, entry_utc, vol_window and max_delay_min from p. (9) Report gotobi and non-gotobi days separately.
